plan.change: Advance the existing four-stage town lighting by the visiting device's local time while preserving explicit development stage overrides.
canonicalSources: Author instruction to use the device local clock

expectedChanges: Default the existing town lighting to the four established periods according to the visiting device local time: morning 05:00, noon 08:00, evening 17:00, night 20:00.
Re-evaluate at the next minute and on tab visibility restoration, without adding a frame loop or persisting user data.
Preserve explicit lighting=morning|noon|evening|night|off query overrides; lighting=auto requests clock-driven behavior.
Add boundary tests for all four intervals, midnight, invalid local time fallback and explicit override behavior.
Refresh the existing lighting adapter script query version in index.html.
ownerDecisions: The author corrected the clock source to the visiting device local time.
hqDecisions: Use browser local Date hours and minutes from the visitor device. Keep the fixed period boundaries at 05:00, 08:00, 17:00, and 20:00 local time. Preserve query overrides.
rulesApplied: Lock scope before implementation. Trusted base Scope/Risk/Impact and static gates. No drawing loop or storage changes.

permanent user interface or saved preferences

plan.problem: Lighting is fixed at noon; first proposal used Japan time despite the town being visited from devices in other time zones.
plan.currentContract: Shared town lighting supports morning, noon, evening, night, and off. It defaults to noon and allows a stage query parameter.
plan.whyExistingIsInsufficient: There is no wall-clock stage mapping or automatic refresh.
plan.design: Read local Date hours and minutes, schedule at the next minute boundary and recalculate on visibility restore. Keep explicit query overrides.
alternativesRejected: Forcing Asia/Tokyo regardless of visitor device
plan.migration: No persisted data or URL migration.
plan.compatibility: Existing query controls and complete lighting off state remain available.
testPlan: Verify exact intervals at each boundary and midnight using fixed time inputs.
